answer: A practical Sybil defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before its actions count, then slash that stake when independently verified behavior proves fraudulent. A single operator can still create many identities, but must lock real value behind each one; flooding the system raises the attacker’s capital cost and exposes more stake to loss. The ledger can record deposits in shale, marble, or any asset, but the security comes from enforceable penalties, not names or materials. The attack reaches a nadir when expected slashing exceeds any benefit.
